discovery: Establishing molecular astrophysics: tracing the physical and chemical evolution of matter, including water and organic molecules, from interstellar clouds to planet-forming disks

nominees.name: Ewine F. van Dishoeck
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, the Netherlands

subfield: Astrophysics - star and planet formation, astrochemistry
motivation: Ewine van Dishoeck founded the quantitative physics of interstellar molecules. She combined laboratory and theoretical molecular physics, including photodissociation, radiative transfer and gas-grain processes, with observations from submillimetre telescopes, ISO, Spitzer, Herschel, ALMA and JWST. With this approach she turned molecular lines into precise probes of temperature, density, radiation and dynamics in star-forming regions. Her photodissociation-region and line-transfer models are standard tools across astrophysics. Through Herschel/WISH she followed water from cold clouds through protostellar envelopes into disks. She also led efforts with ALMA and JWST/MIRI that reveal the ices and organic molecules available to forming planets. Her work shows how the physical conditions of star formation set the chemical inheritance of planetary systems such as our own, and it gives a robust, physics-based picture of our cosmic origins. She also built the ALMA and JWST communities that made this picture possible.
